title: Imitation Learning from Human Motion Alone Does Not Guarantee Biomechanically Plausible Gait Kinetics
abstract: arXiv:2603.12408v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Imitation learning (IL) via motion data is increasingly used in robotics and character animation, yet its ability to be applied to human biomechanics to estimate physiologically plausible joint moments without explicit kinetic information remains unclear. In this study, we examined whether motion imitation alone can estimate reasonable biological joint moments in human walking. We compared motion-only IL (MOIL) against a kinetics-aware IL (KAIL) framework, which incorporates additional ground reaction forces (GRFs) and center of pressure (CoP) in imitation rewards. A progressive kinetic reward shaping approach was used to examine the contribution of each kinetic term. Experiments were conducted using walking data from two non-disabled participants at three speeds (0.9, 1.2, and 1.5 m/s). While both MOIL and KAIL achieved comparable kinematic tracking accuracy, KAIL produced kinetics more closely aligned with biomechanical value

translated_title: 仅依靠人体运动数据的模仿学习并不能保证生物力学上合理的步态动力学
translated_abstract: 通过运动数据进行模仿学习在机器人和角色动画领域的应用日益广泛，然而其在人体生物力学中的应用能力——即在缺乏显式动力学信息的情况下估计生理学合理的关节力矩——仍不明确。在本研究中，我们检验了仅靠运动模仿是否能够在人体行走中估计出合理的生物学关节力矩。我们将仅运动的模仿学习（MOIL）与动力学感知的模仿学习（KAIL）框架进行了比较，后者在模仿奖励中纳入了额外的地面反作用力（GRF）和压力中心。我们采用渐进式动力学奖励塑形方法来考察每个动力学项的贡献。实验使用了来自两名无残疾参与者在三种速度（0.9、1.2和1.5 m/s）下的行走数据。结果表明，尽管MOIL和KAIL在运动学跟踪精度上相当，但KAIL产生的动力学结果与生物力学值更为接近。
tldr: 研究发现仅依靠运动数据的模仿学习虽能准确跟踪运动学，却无法估计出合理的关节力矩，而将地面反作用力和压力中心等动力学信息纳入模仿奖励的KAIL框架能产生更符合生物力学的步态动力学。
en_tdlr: Motion-only imitation learning achieves good kinematic tracking but fails to produce biomechanically plausible joint moments, whereas a kinetics-aware IL framework incorporating ground reaction forces and center of pressure yields gait kinetics that better align with biomechanical values.
